newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 21.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 21.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BRUSSELS - The European Commission says it will renew attempts to introduce a European Union-wide ban on all tobacco advertising, following the announcement by the new British government of a national ban. Two-thirds of EU countries have some kind of restrictions on publicity for cigarette companies, but the EU's executive Commission says the effectiveness of these bans is limited in the increasingly integrated European market.

LONDON - Formula One, the world's most glamorous and expensive motor racing event, is looking for new sponsors as a growing number of countries introduce restrictions on tobacco sponsorship. Formula One receives an estimated 100 million pounds ($165.5 million) in sponsorship money from tobacco companies, experts say. But as countries such as Britain, France, Germany and Canada introduce total or partial bans on tobacco advertising, motor racing teams are looking for alternative sponsors.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Barry Diller, chairman of HSN Inc, parent of the Home Shopping Network, says he expects electronic commerce to grow into a large business in the next several years. "The wind is at the back of electronic commerce," says Diller. "In the next several years, the ability to offer it to others, we believe, is a truly large business."
PARIS - The Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel, the French broadcasting regulator, says it plans a tender for partial licenses to operate some 300 FM radio frequencies.

RESTON, Virginia - Nine Internet service providers say they have formed, a group committed to making the commercial Internet more reliable. The founding members are ANS Communications, AT&T Corp, BBN Corp, EarthLink Network Inc, GTE Corp, MCI Communications Corp, NETCOM On-Line Communications Inc, PSINet Inc and UUNET, a unit of WorldCom Inc.

LONDON - Britain's General Cable Plc, a provider of telecoms services and cable television, says its financial results are on track for the rest of the year. General Cable says it expects to begin trials of new programming packages in the third quarter and implement the most attractive ones in the final quarter.

SHANGHAI - Wuxi CCTV Film and Television Productions Co Ltd, a subsidiary of China Central Television (CCTV), will issue 50 million A shares in an initial public offering, the company says. Proceeds will be used to expand CCTV's production base in Wuxi, in the province of Jiangsu, and for shooting more television series adapted from ancient Chinese classics.

SYDNEY - Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp may still be in breach of broadcasting rules even if it cuts its economic interest in Australia's Ten television network to 57.5 percent from its current 76 percent, the Australian Broadcasting Authority says.
LONDON - British regional newspaper publisher Adscene Group Plc says talks on the sale of its commercial printing division have concluded and the division will remain with the group.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

CHICAGO - McDonald's Corp may have to change the recipe for its U.S. fast-food business. After pursuing dramatic expansion over the past several years, McDonald's must sharpen its focus on product quality and speed up its decision-making to improve sales and profits in the United States, industry analysts say.

HANOI - Germany's Brauhaase Holding (Pacific) Ltd and two local partners have been granted a licence to build a $120-million beer factory in central Vietnam, a Ministry of Planning and Investment official says. The brewery, which will be located in Nghe An province, would have an annual production capacity of 100 million litres.

LONDON - Sir Ian Prosser, chairman of British pub-to-hotel group Bass Plc, says conditions in Germany and France had reached their low point and are now on their way back up. "Germany and France have probably bottomed out and are now on the way back up, and in America we are continuing to see good economic growth," Prosser says.

ANCHORAGE, Alaska - Alaska's commercial salmon season opened with Prince William Sound fishermen hauling in more than six times the anticipated number of Copper River sockeyes, state officials say. The large harvest is likely to depress prices for the Copper River salmon, prized for their strong taste and rich red color and mostly sold to domestic markets, says a spokesman for the Alaska Department of Fish and Game.

AUCKLAND - Investors are queueing for a slice of the action in a rare initial public offering involving the spin-off of Pepsico Inc's New Zealand restaurant chains. The new company, Restaurant Brands New Zealand Ltd, is due to list on June 4. New York-based Pepsico will be selling a free-standing company that controls 122 KFC and Pizza Hut stores across New Zealand.
PARIS - French tobacco company Seita should post "satisfactory" operating profit this year despite losing market share to lower-priced products, Seita chairman Jean-Dominique Comolli says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW ORLEANS - A national poll showing crime threatens the level of tourism in New Orleans is released just hours after a Kentucky tourist was gunned down in the French Quarter during a robbery attempt. The Gallup survey indicated crime has not had a significant impact on the city's tourism business, but it suggested convention organizers were beginning to view New Orleans as unsafe and dirty when compared to regional competitors like San Antonio, Atlanta and Dallas.

SANTIAGO - An American millionaire who bought a wilderness area the size of Rhode Island in southern Chile says he hopes to turn the land into a Chilean national park, despite hostility from local officials. Douglas Tompkins, multi-millionaire founder of the Esprit clothing chain, says he was surprised at the lack of support in President Eduardo Frei's government for his project to create a vast nature reserve of forests, fjords and mountains.

NEW YORK - Credit card users will soon have the option of gazing onto the painted faces and lizard tongues of rock group KISS each time they charge a meal or pay for their purchases in plastic. Wilshire Financial, an entertainment merchant bank in Los Angeles, says it will begin marketing a Visa classic card featuring the band "in full makeup surrounded by a ring of fire."
